2026 United States Senate election in South Carolina

Source: R/data.R
SC26SE.Rd

This is a simple data set on the results of the 2026 United States Senate election in South Carolina.

Usage

SC26SE

Format

A data frame with 2185 rows and 17 columns

long

a longitude coordinate

lat

a latitude coordinate

group

identifies the polygon to which a coordinate belongs

order

an integer that determines the sequence in which coordinates are connected

county

a county name for South Carolina

aan

the number of votes Annie Andrews received in the county

aap

the percentage of votes Annie Andrews received in the county

dgn

the number of votes Darline Graham received in the county

dgp

the percentage of votes Darline Graham received in the county

mn

the vote margin in the count of votes in the county (Andrews' count minus Graham's count)

mp

the vote margin in the percentage of votes in the county (Andrews' count minus Graham's count)

tv

the total number of votes cast in the Senate race in the county

pop

the estimated county population size from 2025

area

the area of the county (in square kilometers)

whitep

the percentage of the county that is white, non-hispanic, per the 2020 Census

blackp

the percentage of the county that is black, non-hispanic, per the 2020 Census

mcat

a factor categorizing the percentage vote margin

Details

This is a Wikipedia scrape job from Nov. 18, 2026. It stands to reason this information is not 100% of all votes cast, but the counting has just about stopped completely and the outcome of the race is already known prior to creating these data.

The mcat column has values of "<= -20", "-20 to -10", "-5 to <0", ">0 to 5", "5 to 10", "10 to 20", and ">= 20". Intervals are left-closed (e.g. [5, 10), [10, 20)) and not the default right-closed. This doesn't matter so much in cases like these as you will never observe actual integers in data like these, nor will you observe actual zero.
